h1: An AI phone host for Mediterranean and Greek restaurants
seoTitle: AI phone answering for Mediterranean and Greek restaurants
description: ROAL is a phone host for Mediterranean and Greek restaurants. It answers calls, takes pickup orders, handles menu questions, and sends kitchen tickets.
lead: Busy lunch and dinner lines can get messy fast at a Mediterranean or Greek restaurant. ROAL answers the phone, takes pickup orders from your live menu, and keeps the front counter moving.
question: How can ROAL handle AI phone answering for Mediterranean and Greek restaurants and take pickup orders correctly?
answer: ROAL is a phone host made for restaurants like Mediterranean and Greek spots. It answers calls, takes pickup and delivery orders from your live menu, handles hours, address, parking, and menu questions, and sends a clean ticket to the kitchen screen. It can also pass along allergy-sensitive questions, complaints, or manager requests to staff.

pains.title: The phone rings during lunch rush
pains.body: A line at the counter and a grill full of gyros can make phone calls pile up. That means missed pickup orders for hummus, shawarma, falafel plates, or Greek salads.

pains.title: Menu questions slow everyone down
pains.body: Callers ask about chicken souvlaki, lamb gyros, vegetarian platters, pita, tzatziki, and whether the fries are gluten-free. Those questions take time when your staff should be packing orders.

pains.title: Busy shifts make order-taking messy
pains.body: On a Friday night, one missed note can mean no onions, extra feta, or tahini on the side. A rushed order can also cause confusion about ready time or which location to pick up from.

howItHelps.title: Answers the phone while your team cooks
howItHelps.body: ROAL picks up calls when the counter is busy, so your staff can focus on the grill, the fryer, and the pickup shelf. It can also take calls only when you are busy or unanswered.

howItHelps.title: Takes real orders from your menu
howItHelps.body: It can capture items, sizes, modifiers, and notes for common Mediterranean and Greek orders. Think chicken shawarma wrap with no onions, gyro plate with extra tzatziki, or spanakopita and a Greek salad.

howItHelps.title: Gives callers the basics fast
howItHelps.body: ROAL can answer questions about hours, address, parking, and menu items. If it cannot answer a question, it can send it to your inbox so you can reply once and the host learns it.

howItHelps.title: Sends a clear ticket to the kitchen
howItHelps.body: Confirmed orders go to the kitchen screen with the caller’s name, phone, items, and ready time. That helps the prep team move faster when the dinner rush starts.

sections.h2: Built for the calls Mediterranean restaurants get all day
sections.body:
Mediterranean and Greek restaurants get the same phone questions over and over. People want pickup for gyro plates, shawarma wraps, falafel, hummus, baba ghanoush, spanakopita, and family platters. They also want to know if there is parking, when lunch starts, and whether a sauce or side can be changed.

ROAL is built for that kind of call. It answers in a warm voice, takes the order, and confirms the details back before sending the ticket to the kitchen. That helps when the front counter is busy with takeout bags and the kitchen is rushing to finish skewers, rice, salad, and pita.

If a caller asks about something sensitive, like an allergy, a large catering tray, or a complaint, ROAL can pass it to staff with a summary. That keeps the call moving without making the guest wait on hold.

sections.h2: What to set up before you go live
sections.body:
Start with a clean menu. Make sure your live menu has the items people actually order by phone: chicken souvlaki, lamb gyro, falafel, Greek salad, rice bowls, pita, tzatziki, and family platters. If you sell specials, note them clearly so the phone host does not guess.

Then check your hours, address, and pickup timing. If your kitchen needs 15 minutes for a wrap and 30 minutes for a family tray, that should be easy to find. ROAL can read your public menu pages, PDF menus, menu photos, or a website. You can also upload a menu if that is easier.

You can test-call the host in the browser before you forward your number. That is useful if you are not tech-heavy and want to hear exactly how it sounds.

sections.h2: A simple way to think about the numbers
sections.body:
ROAL uses pay-per-completed-order pricing. That means the cost is tied to a confirmed order that reaches the kitchen screen, not to every minute the phone rings. There is no monthly fee, no setup fee, and no per-minute fee.

If you want a rough example, say you miss 12 calls on a Friday and 5 of them were pickup orders for gyros, salads, or mezze trays. That is the kind of situation where a phone host can help you capture more of the calls already coming in. It also helps during holiday dinners, weekend rushes, and short-staffed shifts when the phone can pull attention away from the pass.

You can forward all calls, or just unanswered and busy calls, and turn forwarding off any time.

faq.q: Can ROAL take pickup orders for Mediterranean and Greek food without mistakes?
faq.a: ROAL can take items, sizes, modifiers, and notes from your live menu, then read the order back before sending it to the kitchen. It also collects the caller’s name and phone and quotes a ready time. You should still keep your menu current so sold-out items are not offered.

faq.q: Will it answer questions about hummus, gyros, and hours?
faq.a: Yes. It can answer menu, hours, address, and parking questions from the information it reads from your public pages. If it cannot answer something, it sends it to your inbox and learns from your reply.

faq.q: Can it handle allergy questions or complaints?
faq.a: Yes, it can hand off allergy-sensitive questions, complaints, and manager requests to staff with a summary. That is useful when someone asks about sesame, dairy, gluten, or a problem with a previous order.

faq.q: Do I need to replace my restaurant number?
faq.a: No. Your restaurant keeps its own number. You forward calls to ROAL, either all calls or only when busy or unanswered, and you can turn forwarding off any time.

faq.q: What happens if the caller wants to pay by card?
faq.a: ROAL does not take card numbers over the phone. Payment happens at pickup or however your restaurant already takes payment. The host focuses on taking the order and getting it to the kitchen cleanly.
